paragraph.1: I’m Rochenette Legaspina, a UI/UX designer from the Philippines with a Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering. My design approach combines creativity with a focus on user-centered solutions.
paragraph.2: I started my career in the gaming industry, working as a 3D modeler, and later expanded to 3D texturing and re-topology while I was in college. A colleague introduced me to UI/UX design, which sparked my interest in creating user-friendly, creative designs.
paragraph.3: After graduating college, I gained real experience as a UI/UX designer at a software company. Seeking a broader understanding of the development process, I later worked as a Systems Analyst, collaborating closely with clients and team members. This role helped me bridge the gap between design and development, with the goal of creating designs that are both visually appealing and purpose-driven, solving real user problems.

scClaims.title: Senior Citizen Discount Claims System
scClaims.description: SC Claims is a web-based platform that streamlines senior citizen discount validation by allowing users to upload Excel records with SKU details. The system automatically validates these records based on pre-set criteria, ensuring accurate and quick reimbursements to pharmacies and hospitals. By automating this process, SC Claims reduces manual effort, saves time, and ensures a smooth, error-free reimbursement workflow.

hero.description: I'm a Systems Analyst with roots in 3D modeling and UI/UX design. I enjoy designing systems, solving problems, and creating real impact — blending creative intuition with analytical precision to build solutions that are elegant and effective.

about.intro: My career didn't follow a straight line — and that's precisely what makes my perspective unique.
about.chapter1Body: It started with Blender. From getting proportions right to modeling objects from scratch — I worked my way up to baking realistic textures in Substance Painter. That chapter of hands-on 3D work is where it all began, and where I left it to grow further.
about.chapter2Body: From 3D shapes to screen layouts. I moved into Figma and started designing user flows, wireframes, and high-fidelity screens for real products — learning that good design is just as much about how it works as how it looks.
about.chapter3Title: Where I Am Now — Systems Analysis
about.chapter3Body: Before I build anything, I listen — because the right solution means nothing if it's solving the wrong problem. I document requirements, map out business processes, and make sure what the client needs is exactly what gets built — nothing lost between the idea and the product.

books.intro: The titles that fundamentally changed how I think about design, systems, and people.

designOfEverydayThings.insight: Taught me that good design is invisible — when things work, people don't notice the design; they only notice when it fails.

thinkingFastAndSlow.insight: Reframed how I approach user research — understanding that users operate on intuition first, logic second.

atomicHabits.insight: Small, consistent improvements compound over time — you don't rise to your goals, you fall to your systems.

cleanCode.insight: Even as a designer-analyst, understanding clean code principles made me a better systems thinker and collaborator.

leanStartup.insight: Build–Measure–Learn loops shaped how I frame every design and analysis deliverable as a hypothesis to test.
